source.title: Memory or Reasoning? Explore How LLMs Compute Mixed Arithmetic Expressions
source.authors: Chengzhi Li; Heyan Huang; Ping Jian; Zhen Yang; Chen-Xu Wang; Yifan Wang

page_placements.theme: Latent multi-hop and intermediate computation within one forward pass

record.file_problem: none noted; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies internal computation of mixed arithmetic expressions, not whether a state anticipates later tokens or steers intervening text. Its arithmetic-reasoning findings are related but do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study measures arithmetic operand, intermediate-result (IR), and final-result (FR) representations and interventions on arithmetic components. It does not measure future-token decodability, pre-caching for later token positions, rhyme planning, or look-ahead in the listed tasks. Results cited from other work are not counted.
record.test_reason: The study probes how arithmetic operands, intermediate results and final results are represented and routed at the last token of mixed arithmetic expressions in Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. It does not test whether a hidden state encodes tokens several positions ahead, features computed for later positions, rhyme planning, or look-ahead that steers later generation. Its layer-level use of intermediate results is multi-step computation within one forward pass for the next token, not planning ahead. Future Lens (Pal et al., 2023) is cited only in passing in related work, so the relation is cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude neither memory nor reasoning fully applies. The model parses the expression and aggregates operand information at the last token, with no token-level step-by-step computation. For some expressions it relies on intermediate results at the last token, i.e. layer-level arithmetic reasoning. They also propose CEDF fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not apply a future-token anticipation or rhyme-planning method; it uses EAP-IG, Patchscopes, and activation patching to study mixed arithmetic computation.
record.method_sensitivity: The IR/FR resolution trends differ across three expression types and task forms; the text says complex-context forms have lower mean FR resolution rates and greater standard deviation. Knockout effects also differ between m33-heads and m36-heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Within one forward pass at the last token, intermediate arithmetic results become decodable around layer 31. For type-1 expressions they are then converted into the final result. Knocking out m33-heads lowers both IR and FR resolution; knocking out m36-heads lowers FR resolution but not IR resolution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For some mixed arithmetic expressions, LLMs compute intermediate results at the last token across layers and use them to produce the final answer (latent layer-level multi-step computation), rather than computing step by step across tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Findings of ACL 2025)
record.problems: The evidence uses synthetic arithmetic expressions and the authors note limited data diversity, tests only small models of around 10B in the main experiments, does not explore CoT, and uses a single selected expression for the late-head knockout. Several resolution-rate results are presented only in figures; the text gives no numerical uncertainty intervals for the knockout table.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were left out for the 60-row cap. CEDF fine-tuning accuracy results and circuit-performance comparisons were not catalogued because they measure arithmetic-task performance or the study's method, not future-token anticipation or the relevant intermediate-text behavior.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, no frontier model, no rhyme-word intervention.
No decoding of tokens several positions ahead; Patchscopes reads current-answer values at the last token.
No test of features computed at one position for the benefit of later positions.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models.
Multi-step arithmetic is studied within a single next-token prediction; there is no look-ahead to future tokens or moves.
No measurement of plan depth, or of whether plans steer later generation.

record.verdict_notes: The large FR drops (R4, R7, R10, R13) are relabelled observed on the study's own measure; none of the rows links to any claim version. Gemma-2-9B-IT replication results (Figure 18) and Logit Lens checks (Figure 17) exist only as figures; they are also irrelevant to the versions.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or rhyme-directed intervention.
No test of predicting tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.
No test of features computed at one token position because they benefit later positions, or of breadcrumbs.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models or open attribution-graph/probing tools.
No look-ahead test in multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other listed tasks or architectures.
The paper examines arithmetic computation and layer-level IR use, but does not test the depth or causal role of future-token plans, or whether such plans are local heuristics.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Patchscopes resolution-rate measurement of operands, IRs and FRs across layers at the last-token position.

conditions.value: around layer 15 onward; around layer 30 onward

rows.measure: Resolution rate of operand values, IRs and FRs across layers
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that operand resolution gradually decreases from around layer 15 and drops rapidly around layer 30, while IR and FR resolution begins to rise around layer 31. For type-1 expressions, IR resolution later drops as FR resolution rises.
rows.uncertainty: Standard-deviation trend shown as a light area; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: This is decoding of arithmetic values at the last token across layers, not prediction of future tokens or representation at an earlier token position.

source_check.correct: Operand values are resolved at operand positions; intermediate and final results are resolved at the last-token position. Operand resolution decreases from around layer 15 and drops rapidly from around layer 30; intermediate- and final-result resolution rises from around layer 31.
source_check.problem: The operation and condition incorrectly place operand decoding at the last-token position.

tranche.reason: The study measures arithmetic representations and dependencies across layers, without testing or using any listed planning-ahead claim version.
